title: Metagenómica
text: Primero, carguemos MicroBioMeta y tidyverse (usado para el manejo de datos): Cada muestra se procesó por separado, así que los reportes bracken_species se combinaron de antemano en una sola tabla (una columna por muestra, llamada kraken_pluspfp_<id_metagenome>_report_bracken_species) con una columna taxonomy ya agregada como última columna: La taxonomía ya está en la tabla, así que hace falta usar la función merge_feature_taxonomy(). ⚠️ Las cadenas de taxonomía de Kraken2 usan un prefijo k__/p__/c__/… como SILVA/GTDB, pero los rangos están separados por "; " (punto y coma y espacio) en vez de ";". MicroBioMeta ya tiene esto contemplado en cualquier lugar donde exista un argumento taxonomy_db, solo pasa taxonomy_db = "Kraken2". Ahora, carguemos los metadatos: Los nombres de columna de Kraken codifican un número id_metagenome (por ejemplo, kraken_pluspfp_100_report_bracken_species) en vez del ID real de la muestra, así que lo recuperamos con una expresión regular y usamos metadata_meta$id_metagenome para renombrar cada columna su SampleID: Renombremos y demos formato los metadatos: Las coordenadas se tomaron y cargaron así:
code: library("MicroBioMeta") library(tidyverse) table_kraken <- read.delim(     system.file("extdata", "table_kraken.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta"),     row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE )  table_kraken[1:3, c(1:2, ncol(table_kraken))] ##        kraken_pluspfp_100_report_bracken_species ## 101028                                      1302 ## 36050                                        161 ## 56646                                        108 ##        kraken_pluspfp_105_report_bracken_species ## 101028                                      1066 ## 36050                                        345 ## 56646                                        203 ##                                                                                                                  taxonomy ## 101028 k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__pseudograminearum ## 36050               k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__poae ## 56646          k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__venenatum metadata_meta <- read.delim(     system.file("extdata", "metadata_metagenomic.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta"),     check.names = FALSE )  head(metadata_meta[, 1:10]) ##   SAMPLEID id_sequence id_metagenome Poligono Sitio Transecto id_new id_fisicoq ## 1   P1S1T1         111           140        1     1         1     30         30 ## 2   P1S1T2         112           152        1     1         2     13       <NA> ## 3   P1S1T3         113           164        1     1         3     21         21 ## 4   P1S2T1         121           176        1     2         1     11         11 ## 5   P1S2T2         122           188        1     2         2     33      13,33 ## 6   P1S2T3         123           121        1     2         3     12         12 ##   Sites         Names ## 1     1 Tetlanohcan 1 ## 2     1 Tetlanohcan 1 ## 3     1 Tetlanohcan 1 ## 4     2 Tetlanohcan 2 ## 5     2 Tetlanohcan 2 ## 6     2 Tetlanohcan 2 sample_cols <- setdiff(colnames(table_kraken), "taxonomy")  id_metagenome <- as.integer(gsub("kraken_pluspfp_|_report_bracken_species", "", sample_cols))  colnames(table_kraken)[match(sample_cols, colnames(table_kraken))] <-     metadata_meta$SAMPLEID[match(id_metagenome, metadata_meta$id_metagenome)] metadata_meta$Polygon <- factor(paste0("Pol", metadata_meta$Poligono), levels = paste0("Pol", 1:6)) metadata_meta$Site <- as.character(metadata_meta$Sitio) table_meta <- table_kraken[, c(metadata_meta$SAMPLEID, "taxonomy")] coord_meta <- read.csv(     system.file("extdata", "coord_metagenomic.csv", package = "MicroBioMeta") ) %>%     dplyr::select(-Site) %>% # descartamos el índice de sitio general propio del CSV (1-12); queremos `Sitio` (1-2) en su lugar     dplyr::rename(Polygon_num = pol, Site = Sitio) %>%     dplyr::select(Polygon_num, Site, Transecto, Latitude, Longitude)  metadata_meta <- metadata_meta %>%     dplyr::mutate(Polygon_num = as.integer(gsub("Pol", "", Polygon)), Site = as.integer(Site)) %>%     dplyr::left_join(coord_meta, by = c("Polygon_num", "Site", "Transecto")) %>%     dplyr::mutate(Site = as.character(Site))

what: Empezar desde un objeto phyloseq o TreeSummarizedExperiment
title: Metagenómica
text: MicroBioMeta trabaja con tablas simples, pero si tus datos ya están en un objeto phyloseq o en un TreeSummarizedExperiment (el contenedor de Bioconductor que usa la familia de paquetes mia), from_phyloseq() y from_tse() los convierten en la table (con la columna taxonomy al final) y la metadata (con SAMPLEID primero) que usamos en esta viñeta. Para mostrarlo, guardamos la tabla de Kraken2 en un TreeSummarizedExperiment, con una columna de taxonomía por rango, como lo haría mia: from_tse() regresa una lista con los dos data frames: y se pueden usar directo en cualquier función, por ejemplo abundance_bar_plot(table = mbm$table, metadata = mbm$metadata, ...). Con un objeto phyloseq funciona igual:
code: counts <- as.matrix(table_meta[, metadata_meta$SAMPLEID])  ranks <- tidyr::separate(     data.frame(taxonomy = gsub("[kpcofgs]__", "", table_meta$taxonomy)),     taxonomy, c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"),     sep = "; ", fill = "right" ) rownames(ranks) <- rownames(table_meta)  samples <- metadata_meta rownames(samples) <- samples$SAMPLEID  tse <- TreeSummarizedExperiment::TreeSummarizedExperiment(     assays  = list(counts = counts),     rowData = ranks,     colData = samples ) tse ## class: TreeSummarizedExperiment  ## dim: 87 36  ## metadata(0): ## assays(1): counts ## rownames(87): 101028 36050 ... 208348 27350 ## rowData names(7): Kingdom Phylum ... Genus Species ## colnames(36): P1S1T1 P1S1T2 ... P6S2T2 P6S2T3 ## colData names(34): SAMPLEID id_sequence ... Latitude Longitude ## reducedDimNames(0): ## mainExpName: NULL ## altExpNames(0): ## rowLinks: NULL ## rowTree: NULL ## colLinks: NULL ## colTree: NULL mbm <- from_tse(tse, assay_name = "counts")  mbm$table[1:3, c(1:2, ncol(mbm$table))] ##        P1S1T1 P1S1T2 ## 101028   1985   4341 ## 36050     236    231 ## 56646     175    151 ##                                                                                                                  taxonomy ## 101028 k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__pseudograminearum ## 36050               k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__poae ## 56646          k__Eukaryota; p__Ascomycota; c__Sordariomycetes; o__Hypocreales; f__Nectriaceae; g__Fusarium; s__venenatum mbm$metadata[1:3, 1:5] ##   SAMPLEID id_sequence id_metagenome Poligono Sitio ## 1   P1S1T1         111           140        1     1 ## 2   P1S1T2         112           152        1     1 ## 3   P1S1T3         113           164        1     1 mbm <- from_phyloseq(physeq)

text: Misma función que en la viñeta de amplicón; la única diferencia es taxonomy_db = "Kraken2", que le indica la lógica de parseo de taxonomía que espere cadenas estilo Kraken2/Bracken.

text: Los taxones de Kraken2/Bracken son ASVs, así que aquí se usa feature_prefix = "Taxon" en vez del prefijo "ASV" por defecto para las etiquetas de fila. condition2 agrega una segunda barra de anotación, aquí el sitio de muestreo dentro de cada polígono.

title: Metagenómica
text: Como en la viñeta de metabarcoding, primero se puede usar alpha_hill_corr_plot(table = table_meta) para revisar si los números de Hill dependen de la profundidad de secuenciación.

title: Metagenómica
text: fill_col es igual x_col aquí, así que la leyenda solo repetiría las etiquetas del eje x - show_legend = FALSE la quita.  La riqueza (q=0) está casi saturada y plana entre bloques aquí — esta tabla de Bracken nivel de género simplemente tiene mucho margen para variar en q=0 — mientras que q=1 y q=2 (que ponderan por abundancia relativa) sí capturan diferencias entre bloques.
code: alpha_hill_plot(     table = table_meta,     metadata = metadata_meta,     x_col = "Polygon",     fill_col = "Polygon",     facet_by = "Site",     facet_orientation = "horizontal",     legend_title = "",     stat = "kruskal.test",     show_legend = FALSE,     save_table = FALSE )

title: Metagenómica
text: distance = "bray" coincide con el usado en la ordenación de arriba, de modo que la ordenación (vía el paquete vegan (Oksanen et al. 2024)) y la prueba PERMANOVA (Anderson 2001) evalúan la misma noción de disimilitud. El resultado es una figura de la tabla (un ggplot), así que se puede combinar con otros gráficos (p. ej. cowplot::plot_grid()) o guardar con ggplot2::ggsave(). Usa save_table = TRUE para obtener también los resultados en un archivo de texto.
code: beta_test_table(     table = table_meta,     metadata = metadata_meta,     formula_str = "Polygon*Site",     distance = "bray",     test = "permanova",     permutations = 999 )

what: Decaimiento de la similitud comunitaria con la distancia
title: Metagenómica
text: beta_decay_plot() evalúa si las comunidades geográficamente más cercanas también son más similares en composición, mediante una prueba de Mantel (Mantel 1967):  Las comunidades geográficamente más cercanas son significativamente más similares en composición (Mantel r ≈ 0.21, p ≈ 0.001; el valor p exacto varía ligeramente entre corridas ya que la prueba de Mantel se basa en permutaciones), una señal real de decaimiento con la distancia en estos suelos forestales. Sin embargo, la relación es débil: la distancia explica solo cerca del 4 % de la variación en la similitud (R² ≈ 0.04). Se usa bray para ser consistentes con la ordenación de arriba.
code: beta_decay_plot(     table    = table_meta,     metadata = metadata_meta,     lat_col  = "Latitude",     lon_col  = "Longitude",     distance = "bray" )

title: Relative abundance barplot — abundance_bar_plot
text: Generates bar plot relative abundance (%) abundant taxa groups across samples sample groups.

title: Relative abundance barplot — abundance_bar_plot
code: abundance_bar_plot(   table,   metadata = NULL,   taxonomy_db = "silva",   level = "genus",   x_col = NULL,   facet_by = NULL,   width_equal = FALSE,   label = "taxonomy",   top_n = 15,   x_axis_title = "Samples",   y_axis_title = "Relative abundance (%)",   x_label_angle = 0,   strip_text_bold = FALSE,   strip_color = "grey",   aspect_ratio = NULL,   add_remained = FALSE,   save_table = FALSE,   table_filename = "relative_abundance.txt" )

title: Relative abundance barplot — abundance_bar_plot
text: table data frame taxa rows samples columns. last column must named taxonomy, containing full taxonomic strings. metadata data frame containing sample metadata. first column must hold sample IDs (column names table). Optional: NULL (default), one bar drawn per sample. taxonomy_db Character. Database taxonomy strings come : "silva" (default), "gg2" (Greengenes2, also "gg"), "unite" "Kraken2" (also "kraken"). Case-insensitive. level Character. Taxonomic level: "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus" (default) "species". Case-insensitive. x_col Character. Name column metadata x-axis. NULL (default), one bar per sample. facet_by Character. Name column metadata facet plot . Optional; NULL (default) facets. width_equal Logical. TRUE, bars equal width regardless sample count per group. Default FALSE. label Character. Title taxa legend. Default "taxonomy". top_n Integer. Number abundant taxa show. Default 15. x_axis_title Character. Title x-axis. Default "Samples". y_axis_title Character. Title y-axis. Default "Relative abundance (%)". x_label_angle Numeric. Rotation (degrees) x-axis labels. Default 0 (horizontal); use 45 90 overlap. strip_text_bold Logical. TRUE, facet strip labels bold. Default FALSE. strip_color Character. Background color facet strips (used facet_by set). Default "grey". aspect_ratio Numeric. Aspect ratio (height/width) panel. Default NULL (automatic). add_remained Logical. TRUE, adds "" category sum remaining taxa. Default FALSE. save_table Logical. TRUE, saves relative-abundance table tab-delimited file. Default FALSE. table_filename Character. Name path saved file (used save_table = TRUE). Default "relative_abundance.txt".

title: Relative abundance barplot — abundance_bar_plot
text: ggplot object stacked bar plot relative abundances.

title: Relative abundance barplot — abundance_bar_plot
text: Relative abundances calculated per sample (%). Taxa collapsed taxonomic level; taxa resolved level shown "". top top_n taxa shown; others filtered . Samples grouped ordered according x_col. Optional faceting facet_by provided. Features assigned kingdom/domain (e.g. "d__Bacteria;__;__;__;__;__") "Unassigned" removed.

code: abundance_heatmap_plot(   table,   metadata = NULL,   condition1 = NULL,   condition2 = NULL,   condition3 = NULL,   colors_condition1 = NULL,   colors_condition2 = NULL,   colors_condition3 = NULL,   name_legend_condition1 = NULL,   name_legend_condition2 = NULL,   name_legend_condition3 = NULL,   top_n = 15,   exclude_unclassified = TRUE,   cluster = TRUE,   show_column_names = TRUE,   cell_size = NULL,   annotation_height = NULL,   save_table = FALSE,   table_filename = "abundance_heatmap_table.txt",   feature_prefix = "",   max_label_length = 35,   composite_names = TRUE,   draw = TRUE )

title: Heatmap of relative abundance — abundance_heatmap_plot
text: table data frame taxa rows samples columns. last column must named taxonomy, containing full taxonomic strings. metadata data frame containing sample metadata. first column must hold sample IDs (column names table). Optional: NULL (default), heatmap sample annotations. condition1 Character. Name column metadata first column annotation. Optional; NULL (default) none. condition2 Character. Name column metadata second column annotation. Optional; NULL (default) none. condition3 Character. Name column metadata third column annotation. Optional; NULL (default) none. colors_condition1 Optional character vector colors condition1. named, colors matched values name (e.g. c(Roots = "#009E73", Rhizosphere = "#56B4E9")); otherwise assigned alphabetical order values. NULL (default), colorblind-friendly Okabe-Ito palette used. colors_condition2 Optional character vector colors condition2 (rules colors_condition1). NULL (default), colors colorblind-friendly "Safe" palette used, contrast condition1. colors_condition3 Optional character vector colors condition3 (rules colors_condition1). NULL (default), third set colorblind-friendly colors used. name_legend_condition1 Character. Title legend condition1. NULL (default), name condition1 used. name_legend_condition2 Character. Title legend condition2. NULL (default), name condition2 used. name_legend_condition3 Character. Title legend condition3. NULL (default), name condition3 used. top_n Integer. Number abundant features show. Default 15. exclude_unclassified Logical. TRUE (default), taxa classification level ("Unclassified") dropped selecting top_n abundant features, rows identified taxa. Use FALSE keep . cluster Logical. TRUE (default), rows clustered; FALSE, ordered abundance. show_column_names Logical. TRUE (default), sample names shown. cell_size Numeric. Side, millimeters, (square) cell. NULL (default), set automatically. annotation_height Numeric. Height, millimeters, column annotation bar (condition1, condition2, condition3). NULL (default), cell height used. save_table Logical. TRUE, saves abundance table shown heatmap tab-delimited file. Default FALSE. table_filename Character. Name path saved file (used save_table = TRUE). Default "abundance_heatmap_table.txt". feature_prefix Character. Prefix row labels, row number (e.g. feature_prefix = "ASV" labels rows "ASV1", "ASV2"...). Default "" (rows labeled "1", "2"...). max_label_length Integer. Taxon names longer many characters cut ellipsis row labels. NULL never cuts . Default 35. composite_names Logical. TRUE (default), SILVA composite names three genera labeled last genus plus "group" (e.g. "Allorhizobium-Neorhizobium-Pararhizobium-Rhizobium" becomes "Rhizobium group"); two-genus names (e.g. "Escherichia-Shigella") kept whole. full names kept saved table. draw Logical. TRUE (default), heatmap drawn current device. Use FALSE build returned grob without drawing , e.g. combine plots; , unless cell_size given, cells stretch fill panel placed instead fixed size.

text: box one group pair condition1_col, -group comparison (e.g. "Rhizosphere_vs_Roots") can contrasted within-group baseline (e.g. "Rhizosphere_vs_Rhizosphere"): -group turnover higher, groups host distinct communities beyond variability among replicates group. optional condition2_col keeps pairs level (e.g. treatment) facets , comparison confounded .

title: Box plot of pairwise feature turnover (Hill numbers) — beta_turnover_plot
code: table_path <- system.file("extdata", "tabla_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") table <- read.delim(table_path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)  metadata_path <- system.file("extdata", "metadata_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") metadata <- read.delim(metadata_path, check.names = FALSE) colnames(metadata)[1] <- "OTUID"  # comparison_condition1/2 match group pairs regardless of order, so listing # "Rhizosphere_vs_Roots" also catches pairs the self-join recorded the # other way around ("Roots_vs_Rhizosphere") - no need to list both. beta_turnover_plot(     table = table,     metadata = metadata,     comparison_condition1 = c("Rhizosphere_vs_Roots", "Rhizosphere_vs_Rhizosphere"),     comparison_condition2 = c("Control_vs_Control", "Moderate_drought_vs_Moderate_drought"),     condition1_col = "Location",     condition2_col = "Treatment",     facet_colors = c("#5D478B", "#8B668B"),     group_colors = c(         "Rhizosphere_vs_Roots" = "#56B4E9",         "Rhizosphere_vs_Rhizosphere" = "#E69F00"     ) )

title: CCA/RDA biplot — cca_rda_biplot
text: Performs Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) Redundancy Analysis (RDA) abundance table constrained environmental variables, plots samples environmental vectors biplot.

title: CCA/RDA biplot — cca_rda_biplot
code: cca_rda_biplot(   table,   env_data = NULL,   env_vars,   method = "hell",   metadata,   group_col = NULL,   group_colors = NULL,   legend_title = NULL,   scale_env = TRUE,   pval_threshold = 0.05,   p_adjust_method = "none",   show_all_env_vectors = FALSE,   analysis = "CCA",   scale_arrows = 1,   title = "auto",   save_table = FALSE,   table_filename = "cca_rda_scores.txt" )

title: CCA/RDA biplot — cca_rda_biplot
text: table data frame taxa rows samples columns. last column must named taxonomy, containing full taxonomic strings. env_data Optional data frame environmental variables, row names matching sample names table. Default NULL: variables named env_vars taken metadata. Use variables separate table. env_vars character vector names environmental variables (columns metadata, env_data given) include analysis. method Character. Transformation abundances, passed vegan::decostand(). Default "hell" (Hellinger). metadata data frame containing sample metadata. first column must hold sample IDs (column names table). environmental variables can columns metadata (see env_vars). group_col Character. Name column metadata defines groups. Used color samples. Optional; NULL (default) groups. group_colors Optional character vector colors, one per group, named groups order. NULL (default), colorblind-friendly Okabe-Ito palette used. legend_title Character. Title legend. NULL (default), name group_col used. scale_env Logical. TRUE (default), environmental variables scaled (without centering) analysis. pval_threshold Numeric. P-value cutoff (p_adjust_method) draw significant environmental variables. Default 0.05. p_adjust_method Character. Multiple-testing correction vegan::envfit() p-values environmental variables, method stats::p.adjust(). Default "none" (raw p-values), usual choice variables. show_all_env_vectors Logical. TRUE, environmental variables drawn, significant . Default FALSE. analysis Constrained ordination method: "CCA" (default, Canonical Correspondence Analysis) "RDA" (Redundancy Analysis). Case-insensitive. scale_arrows Numeric. Multiplies length environmental arrows; changes drawn. Default 1. title Character. Plot title. "auto" (default) shows "CCA Biplot" "RDA Biplot"; NULL shows title; text used title. save_table Logical. TRUE, saves sample scores environmental vector loadings (one table, type column: "site" "vector") tab-delimited file. Default FALSE. table_filename Character. Name path saved file (used save_table = TRUE). Default "cca_rda_scores.txt".

title: CCA/RDA biplot — cca_rda_biplot
code: table_path <- system.file("extdata", "tabla_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") table <- read.delim(table_path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)  metadata_path <- system.file("extdata", "metadata_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") metadata <- read.delim(metadata_path, check.names = FALSE)  # The environmental variables are columns of metadata, chosen with env_vars cca_rda_biplot(     table                = table,     metadata             = metadata,     env_vars             = c("pH", "TOC", "FW", "Root_FW", "DW"),     analysis             = "RDA",     show_all_env_vectors = TRUE,     group_col            = "Location" )

title: Collapse table — collapse_table
text: Collapses abundance table taxonomic level (e.g. genus, family, phylum), summing counts features share taxonomy. Features resolved level kept . Optionally converts counts relative abundance saves collapsed table.

title: Collapse table — collapse_table
code: collapse_table(   table,   level = "genus",   rel_abun = FALSE,   save_table = FALSE,   table_filename = "collapsed_table.txt" )

title: Collapse table — collapse_table
text: table data frame taxa rows samples columns. last column must named taxonomy, containing full taxonomic strings. columns taken samples, order table. level Character. Taxonomic level: "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus" (default) "species". Case-insensitive. rel_abun Logical. TRUE, converts counts relative abundance (%) per sample. Default FALSE. save_table Logical. TRUE, saves collapsed table tab-delimited file. Default FALSE. table_filename Character. Name path saved file (used save_table = TRUE). Default "collapsed_table.txt".

title: Collapse table — collapse_table
text: list two elements: collapsed_table (wide format, one row per collapsed taxon) long_format (data pivoted one row per taxon/sample combination).

what: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
title: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
text: Computes relative abundance taxa taxonomic level, correlates environmental variables, shows correlations heatmap (tile) bubble plot (circle).

title: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
code: corr_env_abund_plot(   table,   env_data = NULL,   metadata = NULL,   env_vars = NULL,   method = "spearman",   hc.order = TRUE,   geom = c("tile", "circle"),   show_labels = TRUE,   col_palette = NULL,   diverging_palette = "BuOr",   invert_axes = TRUE,   taxonomy_db = "silva",   level = "genus",   pval_threshold = NULL,   p_adjust_method = "BH",   x_label_angle = 45,   save_table = FALSE,   table_filename = "corr.txt" )

title: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
text: table data frame taxa rows samples columns. last column must named taxonomy, containing full taxonomic strings. env_data Optional data frame environmental variables, row names matching sample names table. Default NULL: variables named env_vars taken metadata. Use variables separate table. metadata data frame containing sample metadata. first column must hold sample IDs (column names table). environmental variables can columns metadata (see env_vars). env_vars Character vector environmental variables include correlation analysis (columns metadata, env_data given). Required env_data NULL; separate env_data, NULL uses variables. method Character. Correlation method: "spearman" (default), "pearson" "kendall". hc.order Logical. TRUE (default), taxa variables reordered hierarchical clustering. geom Character. Type visualization generate: "tile" (heatmap, default) "circle" (bubble plot). Case-insensitive. show_labels Logical. TRUE (default), correlation values shown. col_palette Optional character vector colors correlation scale. NULL (default), diverging_palette used. diverging_palette Character. Colorblind-friendly diverging palette, used col_palette NULL: "BuOr" (blue-orange, default), "BuVm" (blue-vermillion), "BuPk" (blue-pink), "GnPk" (green-pink) "PuYl" (purple-yellow); "viridis", sequential scale without neutral midpoint (recommended correlations). invert_axes Logical. TRUE (default), taxa variables swap axes. taxonomy_db Character. Database taxonomy strings come : "silva" (default), "gg2" (Greengenes2, also "gg"), "unite" "Kraken2" (also "kraken"). Case-insensitive. level Character. Taxonomic level: "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus" (default) "species". Case-insensitive. pval_threshold Numeric NULL. P-value cutoff (p_adjust_method) keep taxa significant correlation least one variable. Default NULL (filtering). p_adjust_method Character. Multiple-testing correction p-values taxon x variable correlations, method stats::p.adjust(). Default "BH"; "none" uses raw p-values. x_label_angle Numeric. Rotation (degrees) x-axis labels. Default 45; 0 horizontal labels. save_table Logical. TRUE, saves plotted correlations (one row per taxon variable, raw adjusted p-values) tab-delimited file. Default FALSE. table_filename Character. Name path saved file (used save_table = TRUE). Default "corr.txt".

title: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
text: ggplot object.

title: Correlation between environmental variables and taxa — corr_env_abund_plot
code: table_path <- system.file("extdata", "tabla_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") table <- read.delim(table_path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)  metadata_path <- system.file("extdata", "metadata_bacteria.txt", package = "MicroBioMeta") metadata <- read.delim(metadata_path, check.names = FALSE)  corr_env_abund_plot(     table = table,     metadata = metadata,     env_vars = c("pH", "TOC", "FW", "Root_FW", "DW", "Root_L", "Stem_L"),     method = "pearson",     geom = "tile",     hc.order = FALSE,     invert_axes = TRUE,     show_labels = FALSE,     level = "phylum",     taxonomy_db = "silva" )

title: Convert a phyloseq object to MicroBioMeta tables — from_phyloseq
text: physeq phyloseq object OTU table taxonomy table sample data.

title: Convert a phyloseq object to MicroBioMeta tables — from_phyloseq
text: list two data frames: table Taxa rows, samples columns, last column taxonomy full taxonomic string (e.g. "k__Bacteria; p__Firmicutes; c__Bacilli"). metadata Sample metadata whose first column, SAMPLEID, holds sample names table.

title: Convert a phyloseq object to MicroBioMeta tables — from_phyloseq
code: if (requireNamespace("phyloseq", quietly = TRUE)) {     counts <- matrix(c(10, 0, 5, 3, 8, 1),         nrow = 3,         dimnames = list(c("ASV1", "ASV2", "ASV3"), c("S1", "S2"))     )     tax <- matrix(         c(             "Bacteria", "Bacteria", "Bacteria",             "Firmicutes", "Proteobacteria", NA         ),         nrow = 3, dimnames = list(rownames(counts), c("Kingdom", "Phylum"))     )     samples <- data.frame(         Soil = c("Rhizosphere", "Bulk soil"),         row.names = c("S1", "S2")     )     ps <- phyloseq::phyloseq(         phyloseq::otu_table(counts, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),         phyloseq::tax_table(tax),         phyloseq::sample_data(samples)     )     mbm <- from_phyloseq(ps)     mbm$table     mbm$metadata } #>   SAMPLEID        Soil #> 1       S1 Rhizosphere #> 2       S2   Bulk soil

code: if (requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE)) {     counts <- matrix(c(10, 0, 5, 3, 8, 1),         nrow = 3,         dimnames = list(c("ASV1", "ASV2", "ASV3"), c("S1", "S2"))     )     tax <- data.frame(         Kingdom = "Bacteria",         Phylum = c("Firmicutes", "Proteobacteria", NA),         row.names = rownames(counts)     )     samples <- data.frame(         Soil = c("Rhizosphere", "Bulk soil"),         row.names = c("S1", "S2")     )     se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(         assays = list(counts = counts), rowData = tax, colData = samples     )     mbm <- from_tse(se)     mbm$table     mbm$metadata } #>   SAMPLEID        Soil #> 1       S1 Rhizosphere #> 2       S2   Bulk soil

title: MicroBioMeta 0.99.0
text: NEW FEATURES Added NEWS.md file track changes package. Bundled real (subset) 16S example dataset inst/extdata (tabla_bacteria.txt / metadata_bacteria.txt), used throughout documentation examples. SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES aldex_heatmap_plot(): saved table, column seccion (group taxon higher) now named higher_in. aldex_volcano_plot() aldex_heatmap_plot() gain mc_samples, number ALDEx2 Monte Carlo instances. default, 128 (ALDEx2’s default), gives results ; fewer instances faster (e.g. 16 quick look) less stable. ancombc_plot() 2.5 times faster: longer runs ANCOMBC2 sensitivity analysis (pseudo_sens), plot use. plotted taxa ; saved table longer passed_ss_* diff_robust_* columns. abundance_heatmap_plot(): top_n now defaults 15, abundance_bar_plot() (default). beta_partition_ord_plot(): group_col required (dispersion lines centroid computed per group; , NULL default failed unclear error), table_filename defaults "beta_partition" (files beta_partition_jacs.txt, _jtus.txt, _jnes.txt) instead "SAMPLE1". venn_plot(): merge_by required (NULL default failed unclear error). taxonomy_db level work way every function : accepted values aliases ("silva", "gg2"/"gg", "unite", "Kraken2"/"kraken"; kingdom species, case-insensitive) clear error anything else. ratios_bubble_plot() now names taxa like abundance_bar_plot() every level every database (, level = "species" worked Kraken2, class, order family kept full taxonomy string). abundance_sankey_plot() defaults taxonomy_db = "silva", like functions. alpha_hill_corr_plot(): title = "auto" (default) shows default title NULL shows none, beta_ord_plot() cca_rda_biplot() (, "default" "none"). collapse_table() longer takes metadata (used order sample columns): keeps every sample column table, order. Call collapse_table(table, level = ...). cca_rda_biplot() corr_env_abund_plot() take environmental variables directly metadata: env_data now optional (default NULL) env_vars names metadata columns use, need build separate table row names sample order. separate env_data table still works . abundance_bar_plot() abundance_heatmap_plot() longer need metadata: without (without x_col), show one bar column per sample. Passing something table (e.g. R’s table() function mistake) now gives clear error. beta_ord_plot() beta_test_table() gain mc_samples distance = "compositional": number ALDEx2 Monte Carlo instances. 1 (default) uses one random instance, , one drawn (15x faster; seed values differ previous version, drew 128 used first). Values 1 average clr values instances (e.g. 128, ALDEx2’s default), gives stable results runs. Faster, identical results: corr_env_abund_plot() computes correlation p-values pairs (values cor.test()), abundance_heatmap_plot() reads taxonomy string , beta_turnover_plot() computes pairwise Hill partition matrices (values hillR::hill_taxa_parti_pairwise(); 134 s -> 1 s 53 samples), package theme built per session. SILVA composite genus names three genera now shown “ group” (e.g. “Allorhizobium-Neorhizobium-Pararhizobium-Rhizobium” becomes “Rhizobium group”) abundance_heatmap_plot(), abundance_bar_plot(), abundance_sankey_plot(), aldex_heatmap_plot() aldex_volcano_plot(); two-genus names (e.g. “Escherichia-Shigella”) kept whole. abundance_heatmap_plot() also cuts labels longer max_label_length gains composite_names turn rule . abundance_heatmap_plot(): annotation tiles size heatmap cells; named colors_condition* matched name; condition 2 defaults colorblind-friendly “Safe” palette; new draw argument (heatmap drawn ; draw = FALSE builds grob fills panel placed , e.g. cowplot::plot_grid()). Printing returned object draws heatmap. aldex_heatmap_plot() now filters taxa like aldex_volcano_plot() default: pval_threshold = 0.05 effect_threshold = 0 (: |effect| >= 0.8 p-value filter), show taxa. Old argument names (e.g. col_cond, env_table, index) longer accepted; functions longer take ..., misspelled old argument name gives R’s usual “unused argument” error. aldex_heatmap_plot() now returns grob (instead ComplexHeatmap::HeatmapList) can combined plots (e.g. cowplot::plot_grid()) drawn printed; new draw argument; effect_colors takes 3 plain colors pvalue_colors named vector (previous forms still work). abundance_sankey_plot() longer writes HTML file default (output_file = NULL) gains width/height. Standardized optional table-export interface across plotting processing functions: every function now uses save_table/table_filename (default FALSE) instead previous, inconsistent argument names (e.g. export_txt/file_name). Renamed example metadata column Type_of_soil Location, recoded Treatment numeric codes (1/2/3) descriptive labels (Control, Moderate_drought, Severe_drought). beta_ord_plot() now displays NMDS stress value plot ordination = "NMDS". beta_test_table() now labels betadisper output actual grouping variable name instead vegan’s generic "Groups" label. Added panel_label_case/panel_labels/panel_label_bold arguments multi-panel plotting functions journal-style figure labeling, removed hardcoded letter prefixes (./b./c.) lollipop-style plots. Ratio lollipop plots now share consistent visual style, legend titles derived dynamically chosen condition column instead hardcoded. Genus/species-level taxon labels now italicized across plots. BUG FIXES beta_ord_plot() works without group_col (points one color); failed although group_col defaults NULL. Fixed ancombc_plot() heatmap (3+ groups) centering color scale middle LFC range instead 0, made small negative log fold changes look enriched. White now LFC = 0, symmetric limits. Fixed crash abundance_heatmap_plot() phylum annotation contained NA values, 8 groups requested RColorBrewer, annotation columns numeric. Fixed bug corr_env_abund_plot() (taxon ...) loop variable shadowed taxon object used downstream, causing auto_copy(): x y must share src error. Fixed taxonomy columns dropped unintentionally beta_turnover_plot(). Fixed italic formatting Hill-number (q0/q1/q2) facet labels beta_turnover_plot(). Fixed beta_partition_ord_plot()’s shape legend showing raw (!.null(shape_col)) ... R expression title instead column name, color/shape legends overlapping panel titles (legend.box now horizontal instead stacking vertically). Fixed aldex_volcano_plot()’s “Lower/Higher <condition>” corner labels backwards hjust values, pushed text past panel edge clipped ; ’re now anchored stay fully inside panel. Fixed beta_ord_plot()’s taxon-loading labels rendering one long unbroken word (e.g. uncultured_Acidobacteriaceae) instead wrapping onto multiple lines, added "metagenome" placeholder taxonomy strings excluded vector labels. Fixed aldex_heatmap_plot() row (taxon) names never rendering despite underlying data correct - ComplexHeatmap’s built-row-name mechanism wasn’t drawing anything composite annotation layout, row labels now drawn via explicit anno_text() row annotation instead; genus-level names italicized, higher-rank fallback labels (e.g. "Chytridiomycetes") . Fixed beta_turnover_plot() printing hillR’s raw pairwise-comparison progress bar straight console/output. Standardized package’s 2-group default color pair (.mbm_colors_2group, used alpha_hill_plot(), alpha_diversity_plot(), beta_dissimilarity_plot(), beta_ord_plot(), venn_plot(), others) use light blue qualitative 3+-group palette, instead separate darker navy - group’s color longer changes shade depending whether ’s plotted alongside 1 3+ groups. Fixed duplicate, empty Alpha diversity section _pkgdown.yml’s reference index. Fixed stale references pre-rename function names (alpha_hill_corrplot -> alpha_hill_corr_plot, beta_partition_plot -> beta_partition_ord_plot) left code comments one @param doc. Fewer dependencies: reshape2, purrr, tidyselect, RColorBrewer viridis removed Imports (uses now done tidyr, base R scales, identical results). Code restyled 4-space indentation (styler). Removed install.packages() calls within functions; missing Suggested/Imported packages now fail informative stop() message instead installing silently, per Bioconductor guidelines. Removed assign(..., envir = .GlobalEnv) side effects; functions return results directly. Replaced T/F literals TRUE/FALSE, 1:length(x)-style indexing (breaks zero-length input) seq_along()/seq_len(). Added Depends: R (>= 4.1) floor DESCRIPTION, reflecting package’s use native lambda (\(x) ...) syntax. Removed shared_plot() beta_plot_flexible(), two unexported unused legacy functions superseded beta_dissimilarity_plot(). Added x_label_angle, strip_text_bold, aspect_ratio arguments alpha_hill_plot(), alpha_diversity_plot(), beta_dissimilarity_plot(), beta_turnover_plot(), abundance_bar_plot() consistent control tick-label rotation, facet strip weight, panel proportions across package’s bar/boxplot functions. Added stat argument beta_dissimilarity_plot() beta_turnover_plot() optional ggpubr::stat_compare_means() statistical comparison, matching alpha diversity plotting functions. Added label_size filter_uncultured arguments aldex_volcano_plot().
